entries.proposed_fact: Paid witness fees of $1.49 in the first Levin Sockum trial and $2.24 in the second trial (Apr 14, 1856), in which she was again named as a witness
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed p. 36 / PDF p. 52
entries.notes: MERGE DEPENDENCY: stage to canonical 9334 only; duplicate 11251 merge is held under ARCHIVE_MERGE_PROPOSAL_9334.md; 7577 (Lydia Clark) is a separate person and gets none of these facts. OVERLAP-adjacent: her 1855 testimony is already staged in archive_enrichment_ingestion.json; the fees and the second-trial appearance are new.

entries.proposed_fact: A monument erected in 1927 by the Society of Colonial Dames at Oak Orchard names her Nau-gwo-od-wa and honors her as the last Nanticoke speaker in Delaware and Eastern Maryland
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 38-39 / PDF pp. 54-55
entries.notes: MERGE DEPENDENCY: stage to canonical 9334 only; duplicate 11251 merge is held under ARCHIVE_MERGE_PROPOSAL_9334.md; 7577 (Lydia Clark) is a separate person and gets none of these facts. The 'last speaker' wording is the monument's own text, recorded as monument wording, not as a settled linguistic fact. The Indian name corroborates that duplicate profile 11251 (Lydia Nau-Gwa-Ok-Wa Norwood Clark) is the same person.

entries.source_ref: Forgotten Folk, trial narrative and Clark family chapter
entries.proposed_fact: Her maiden name was Norwood and she was a sister to Noke Norwood; on cross-examination she identified herself in relation to Noke Norwood: 'I would a been [his brother] if God almighty hadn't of made a mistake and made me a woman'
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed p. 35 / PDF p. 51 and printed p. 89 / PDF p. 109
entries.notes: MERGE DEPENDENCY: stage to canonical 9334 only; duplicate 11251 merge is held under ARCHIVE_MERGE_PROPOSAL_9334.md; 7577 (Lydia Clark) is a separate person and gets none of these facts. Maiden name is consistent with the archive name Lydia E Norwood. The sister statement rests on her own cross-examination plus a Nanticoke informant's statement to Weslager. Noke Norwood's candidate profile 10458 (Noble Norwood) was not independently verified in this staging.

entries.proposed_fact: Mother of W. R. Clark; when representatives of the Canadian Nanticoke returned, they visited her at Indian River and were entertained by her son
entries.citation: Speck, The Nanticoke Community of Delaware (1915), printed pp. 8-9 / PDF pp. 20, 23
entries.notes: MERGE DEPENDENCY: stage to canonical 9334 only; duplicate 11251 merge is held under ARCHIVE_MERGE_PROPOSAL_9334.md; 7577 (Lydia Clark) is a separate person and gets none of these facts. New to 9334: no kinship fact is staged for her in the claim-audit set. W. R. Clark's own archive identity is unresolved (allocation map, Tier D), but the relationship fact attaches to Lydia regardless of which Clark profile is his. CONFLICT, not staged here and not resolved: Speck dates a Lydia Clark's death to 'probably between 1840 and 1850' (printed p. 9 / PDF p. 23), against her recorded death on 26 Dec 1856; carried as a conflict note in the allocation map.

entries.proposed_fact: Owned and operated a small general store in Indian River Hundred; sold a quarter-pound of powder and shot to Isaiah Harmon
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 31-32 / PDF pp. 47-48
entries.notes: OVERLAP: his status as the 1855 trial defendant is already staged in archive_enrichment_ingestion.json; the store operation and this specific sale are new. Profile 11769 (Levin Sockum, undated) is a duplicate-form entry, not a dated rival; the claim-audit staging already chose 1924.

entries.proposed_fact: Tried a second time on Apr 14, 1856, for gun possession; convicted and fined $20 plus costs (the first trial also drew a $20 fine plus costs)
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed p. 36 / PDF p. 52
entries.notes: New beyond the staged fact, which covers only the 1855 trial.

entries.proposed_fact: After the trials he closed his store, moved his family out of Indian River Hundred, and settled in Gloucester, New Jersey
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 36-37 / PDF pp. 52-53
entries.notes: Consistent with the profile's birth 1807 and death 25 Dec 1864, and with the Sockum family's later New Jersey presence.

entries.proposed_fact: Donated the land for the Hollyville School, also called the Norwood School
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed p. 117 / PDF p. 139
entries.notes: Uniqueness: the only Samuel Norwood profile in the index (b. 24 Feb 1829 Millsboro, d. 16 Dec 1907 Indian Mission). Detail file checked: it carries no school fact.

entries.proposed_fact: Named in the 1881 act incorporating the Incorporated Body of the Nanticoke Indians (list entry 'Samuel B. Norwood')

entries.notes: Per-name check done: the name appears in both the Forgotten Folk transcription (printed p. 115 / PDF p. 137) and the Norwood 2007 booklet transcription (printed p. 39) of the 1881 act list, and audit item D12 verified the act itself (16 Del. Laws ch. 359). Middle initial matches the profile exactly; age 52 in 1881. Detail file checked: no 1881 fact present.

entries.proposed_fact: Nanticoke councillor; grandson of the Harmon of the 1855 Levin Sockum case and a descendant of Levin Sockum on his grandmother's side
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 108-110 / PDF pp. 130-132

entries.proposed_fact: Nanticoke craftsman and one of Weslager's informants; demonstrated whittling a corn peg and a 'figger four' trap trigger in minutes; source of the recollection of Ann Johnson's household
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 108-110, 115 / PDF pp. 130-132, 137
entries.notes: The only Oscar Wright profile (b. 1868, d. 1956). Weslager's character adjectives for him are excluded as author assessment; only the role and activity facts are staged. The plate panel 'Oscar Wright, Nanticoke craftsman' (facing printed p. 94) is recorded as book photo evidence only; no archive photo_id is claimed for it.

entries.proposed_fact: Nanticoke chicken raiser (plate caption, Forgotten Folk)
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), PDF p. 95 (plate facing printed p. 76)
entries.notes: Uniqueness: the only Elwood Wright profile of the era (detail file: born 1880, Delaware; 1880 census; Social Security application). William Author Elwood Wright III (8896, b. 1928) is a later namesake. Photo evidence is the book plate itself; no archive photo_id is claimed.

entries.proposed_fact: Son of David Wright; brother of Oscar, Warren, and Walter Wright; father of Reba Wright
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed p. 116 / PDF p. 138 and printed pp. 108-110 / PDF pp. 130-132
entries.notes: Kinship as stated by Weslager. David Wright has no profile (Tier C in the allocation map) and the Warren and Walter identities are Tier D there; the fact is staged on Elwood as the book states it and does not depend on resolving them.

entries.proposed_fact: Possessor of a roughly 100-year-old log corn mortar, grandson and namesake of its original owner; used it himself until about 15 years before Weslager wrote
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 189-190 / PDF pp. 219-220
entries.notes: The only Perry Hughes profile (b. 14 Oct 1865, d. 19 Jan 1941). Detail file checked: no mortar fact present. A date tension affecting a different Perry Hughes mention in the Norwood 2007 booklet's 1943-article chain is recorded in the allocation map and does not touch this Weslager fact.

entries.proposed_fact: Moor informant who fashioned a gourd funnel, water bottle, corn flour sifter, and salt and pepper shakers as examples of early gourd utensils (Figure IV)
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 192-194 / PDF pp. 222-224
entries.notes: The only Levi Mosley profile. The profile's own dates are internally inconsistent (birth Oct 1889 against age 20 in the 1900 census), which does not affect this undated craft fact. Archive portrait photo_id 1742 is a different photograph and is recorded as photo evidence only.

entries.proposed_fact: Present at the Nov 24, 1921 organization meeting in Russel Clark's house
entries.citation: Weslager, Delaware's Forgotten Folk (1943; 2006 paperback), printed pp. 91-92 / PDF pp. 111-112
entries.notes: The only Gardiner Street of the right generation (b. 7 Jan 1877, d. 14 Dec 1955), age 44 in 1921. Gardiner Street Jr. (6075, b. 1914) was 7 and is excluded. Detail file checked: no meeting fact present.
